title: SupplyChain Vendor Onboarding: SLA & Legal Ops Kickoff
next_steps: Redwood to share MSA + DPA redlines matrix by 2025-11-03
SE to run a 48-hour perf benchmark with HarborSupply sample prompts and send results by 2025-11-07
AE to provide draft committed capacity pricing for 6- and 12-month terms by 2025-11-05
Customer to confirm procurement decision committee date (target week of 2025-11-10)
action_items: Maya Chen - assemble redlines matrix & pricing options - due 2025-11-03
Carlos Rivera - perf benchmark (latency/99th/throughput) + runbook for KV-caching test - due 2025-11-07

header:
Date: 2025-10-30 | Start: 16:00 UTC | Duration: 58 min | Platform: Zoom | Recording: enabled
Redwood: Maya Chen (AE), Carlos Rivera (SE) | HarborSupply: Lena Ortiz (Procurement), Tom Park (InfoSec), Aisha Khan (VP Eng), Samir Patel (Finance)
summary: Kickoff to align on vendor onboarding path: MSA/DPA redlines, SLA targets, pricing approvals and a two-week pilot/perf benchmark. InfoSec raised KMS, data residency and audit log concerns; procurement asked for committed capacity pricing and billing cadence. Next steps: redlines matrix, perf test, pricing options, and procurement meeting scheduling.
topics: MSA redlines, DPA data residency, SLA/99th latency targets, committed capacity pricing, KMS/HSM and key control, audit logs, SOC2 artifacts, pilot benchmark plan, billing cadence, procurement timeline
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. We're happy to kick off the onboarding loop with HarborSupply. I'll quickly run the agenda: legal redlines, SLA expectations, pricing paths, and a short pilot/benchmark plan. Carlos and I will take notes.
[00:18] Lena Ortiz: Thanks Maya. We pulled together folks from procurement, finance, security, and engineering so we can close out the gating items. We have internal gate on 11/12 so trying to align.
[00:31] Carlos Rivera: Hi all, Carlos here — I'll lead the technical parts on the pilot and perf. Quick note: when we talk SLA numbers I may use 99th p99 and p95 interchangeably in speech, please flag if you need clarification.
[00:45] Tom Park: Good afternoon. InfoSec things are top of mind: KMS integration, audit logs (retention and tamper evidence), VPC peering or private link options, and DPA clauses for residency.
[01:02] Aisha Khan: For engineering: latency targets under load and deterministic behavior matter more than raw averages. We run bursts around month-end that spike seq lengths; need fallback plan if hosted caps.
[01:16] Maya Chen: Totally, we hear you. Redwood offers Hosted, Dedicated, and Private modes — the policy routing and fallback mechanism can route to dedicated capacity if hosted is saturated. We can document a canary/fallback.
[01:30] Samir Patel: Quick finance question — committed capacity vs pure usage pricing. What's the uplift and are we able to escrow or put bump clauses for overage?
[01:44] Carlos Rivera: For committed pools we typically offer a discount ~18-28% depending on term and GPU profile. Overage is billed at a reduced burst rate; we can show tiered examples.
[01:58] Lena Ortiz: On the MSA/DPA front, legal sent a redline with three must-haves: stricter data residency, audit rights, and some indemnity language. We need to know what Redwood can concede and what's impossible.
[02:12] Maya Chen: Understood. We usually can accept narrower residency options for Dedicated/Private deployments. For hosted we have region guarantees and contractual commitments but full on-prem residency requires Private.
[02:27] Tom Park: For audit logs — we want immutable logs with at least 1 year retention and exportability to our SIEM. Also, KMS integration must allow customer-managed keys or HSM.
[02:41] Carlos Rivera: We support KMS integrations and a bring-your-own-key (BYOK) flow for Private. Hosted can offer envelope encryption with customer KMS for some plans; I'll follow up with exact architecture diagrams.
[02:56] Maya Chen: I'll add that to the redlines matrix. Quick clarification: when you say "immutable", do you mean write-once logs with cryptographic signing, or just tamper-evident exports?
[03:08] Tom Park: Prefer cryptographic signing but tamper-evident exports to our S3 are acceptable as a minimum.
[03:19] Aisha Khan: On performance, we want to run the pilot using a realistic prompt set — 80% short instructions, 20% long context seqs around 2048 tokens. Can Redwood replicate the KV cache warm paths?
[03:33] Carlos Rivera: Yes, we can run KV-cache warmup runs and measure cold vs warm latencies. We'll simulate your seq distribution. Expect us to produce a perf spreadsheet with p50/p95/p99 and token throughput.
[03:47] Lena Ortiz: Who owns the data deletion guarantees? Our data retention policy mandates deletion within 7 days of request for test data and 30 days for logs unless otherwise retained for compliance.
[04:00] Maya Chen: For Hosted, we offer configurable retention windows and contract terms to cover deletion; Dedicated/Private have more control. We'll flag standard deletion SLA clauses in the DPA and where we can't meet it.
[04:13] Samir Patel: On billing cadence — monthly vs quarterly vs annual. Do you accept net-30 terms and can you do invoiced pay with PO?
[04:26] Maya Chen: Yes, we accept PO-based invoicing on enterprise agreements, common terms are net-30 or net-45; for larger committed contracts we can discuss net-60 with credit checks.
[04:39] Tom Park: Back on SLA: what's Redwood's standard latency SLA? We need p95 under 450ms for short prompts in hosted mode; is that realistic?
[04:52] Carlos Rivera: For short prompts on modern LLMs on hosted with our GPU fleet, p95 around 200-400ms is typical depending on model and region. P99 is harder at scale; with Dedicated you get tighter tail control.
[05:07] Aisha Khan: Is there an option for preemptive burst capacity if we hit month-end traffic?
[05:15] Maya Chen: Yes, we have burst capacity options — you can configure autoscale policies with guaranteed commit and short-term burst lanes. We document burst pricing separately.
[05:28] Lena Ortiz: Legal question: indemnity and liability caps. Our counsel pushed for lower limits given PII processing. Is there wiggle room?
[05:39] Maya Chen: We can discuss incremental caps tied to committed spend. For higher liability profiles we recommend Private deployments plus elevated SLAs and insurance.
[05:51] Tom Park: Regarding encryption in transit and at rest, do you provide TLS1.3 and field-level encryption?
[05:59] Carlos Rivera: Yes TLS 1.3 in transit, and field-level or application-level encryption can be implemented on Private deployments; hosted supports envelope encryption. We'll surface the specifics in the security pack.
[06:11] Aisha Khan: Can we see SOC2 Type II and any penetration test reports?
[06:17] Maya Chen: Absolutely — we'll provide SOC2 attestation and a recent pentest summary under an NDA. I'll drop the access link.
[06:26] Lena Ortiz: About the MSA, our legal redline also requests a 60-day termination without cause with pro-rated refund for unused commitment. Is that standard?
[06:38] Maya Chen: Typical Redwood MSA has a 90-day termination for convenience for enterprise customers, but we can discuss pro-rated refund terms on a case-by-case basis for committed capacity. I'll put that on the redlines matrix.
[06:52] Samir Patel: If we commit for 12 months, what's the onboarding SLA? We need production-ready within 4 weeks.
[07:01] Carlos Rivera: For Dedicated deployments we can often onboard in 2-4 weeks depending on region and infra approvals. Private/on-prem takes longer — usually 6-10 weeks. We'll map the process.
[07:15] Aisha Khan: Any network egress costs we need to be aware of? Our infra team is sensitive to cross-region egress.
[07:23] Maya Chen: Egress is billed separately as per region — we'll include typical egress scenarios in the cost model. For Private/VPC residency, egress can be minimized.
[07:36] Tom Park: About DPA: we need standard SCCs referenced and clauses for subprocessors and notification timelines for breaches — 72 hours.
[07:48] Maya Chen: Redwood adheres to standard breach notification windows in DPA; 72-hour notification is in line with our practice. We'll point to the DPA section with subprocessors listed.
[08:00] Carlos Rivera: Quick technical point — when we cite "KV cache" in architecture, sometimes transcribers write it as K V cash; forgive the transcript. We'll include a clear diagram.
[08:10] Lena Ortiz: (laughs) Noted. Also we have to run this by our payments team for escrow options — any precedent for escrowed credits?
[08:22] Maya Chen: We have used escrow arrangements in a couple of enterprise scenarios; it's doable with the right legal paperwork.
[08:33] Samir Patel: Are there export controls or restricted data considerations? We handle some regulated PII for EU customers.
[08:41] Tom Park: Also data residency must be EU for EU-sourced PII; we might require EU-only hosting for those workloads.
[08:50] Maya Chen: We can lock routing to EU regions and limit model variants to those in-region for residency. We'll add that as a policy example in the redlines doc.
[09:02] Aisha Khan: For the pilot, what is the expected artifact set? We want logs, latency traces, and cost-per-1k tokens estimates.
[09:12] Carlos Rivera: We'll provide a perf spreadsheet, raw trace dumps (obfuscated if necessary), and a cost model for productionized prompt mix. We'll include tokenized counts.
[09:23] Lena Ortiz: Any chance we can get an example SLA with remediation credits for downtime? Our procurement requires a service credit table in the contract.
[09:33] Maya Chen: Yes the MSA has a Service Level Exhibit with credits mapped to outage duration and severity — we can circulate the standard exhibit and mark items you want changed.
[09:45] Samir Patel: On price approvals, is there room for a blended rate across models if we hit a certain token threshold? We want predictability.
[09:55] Carlos Rivera: We can propose a blended committed rate with model buckets — e.g., standard open-model bucket vs high-performance bucket. We’ll show a sample blended pricing schedule.
[10:06] Tom Park: Regarding pen tests, will Redwood allow us to run a scoped pen test against dedicated endpoints post-onboarding?
[10:15] Maya Chen: Scoped pen testing on Dedicated is typically allowed after onboarding and with an agreed test window and rules of engagement — we'll coordinate.
[10:27] Aisha Khan: On the topic of redlines — our legal flagged two specific clauses: (1) data processing sublimit for liability, (2) audit inspection scope. Are those negotiable?
[10:38] Maya Chen: We'll put both in the matrix and flag which are standard vs not recommended. Liability sublimits tied to committed spend are easier to negotiate. Audit inspection scope we'll map to what we can reasonably provide — e.g., SOC2 + on-prem inspection for Private.
[10:53] Lena Ortiz: Great. Let's talk timeline then. We need redlines and pricing by 11/03 to prep the procurement packet for 11/10 meeting. Can Redwood meet that?
[11:03] Maya Chen: Yes, that's doable. I'll own the MSA/DPA redlines deliverable and Carlos will own perf artifacts.
[11:13] Carlos Rivera: For the perf test we need a sample prompt set and expected concurrency — can HarborSupply share a sanitized subset?
[11:22] Aisha Khan: We'll prepare a 200-prompt set and expected concurrency profile (avg 150 concurrent calls during spikes). We'll share by Friday.
[11:33] Tom Park: Also sending our compliance checklist and required artifacts.
[11:39] Maya Chen: Excellent. Any other blockers we didn't cover?
[11:44] Lena Ortiz: Just one: is there pre-signed NDA or is the current engagement covered? We prefer an outbound mutual NDA before sharing pentest or internal docs.
[11:54] Maya Chen: We have an updated mutual NDA — I'll send it after the call for signature.
[11:59] Samir Patel: One more — do you provide cost forecasting tools in the console for committed vs usage?
[12:07] Carlos Rivera: Yes, Redwood Console has cost projections, token-level breakdowns, and forecast exports; we can enable a read-only account for your FinOps.
[12:16] Aisha Khan: About rollout: if we start with Hosted pilot and then move to Dedicated, is the model pinning and KV cache migration smooth?
[12:26] Carlos Rivera: Yes, we support pinning model versions and migration paths; KV cache warming across environments needs a short seeding process but is supported. We'll document the steps.
[12:39] Maya Chen: Alright quick recap: Redwood will deliver MSA/DPA redlines matrix by 11/03, committed capacity pricing options by 11/05, perf benchmark (with p50/p95/p99) by 11/07, and security artifact links/ NDA. HarborSupply will share sanitized prompt set and compliance checklist by end of week.
[12:58] Lena Ortiz: That matches our notes. Thanks — we'll aim to have procurement committee date by Monday next week.
[13:05] Tom Park: We'll review the SOC2 and send any follow-ups on KMS architecture.
[13:12] Maya Chen: Perfect. I'll follow up with an email summarizing redlines and attach the MSA exhibit and security pack. Thanks everyone.
[13:20] -- End of recording (approx 58 minutes)

Notes on transcript quality: medium — occasional mis-attributions and some technical terms mis-transcribed (KV cache -> K V cash). There was brief crosstalk at 09:45.

References mentioned: MSA (Master Service Agreement), DPA (Data Processing Agreement), SOC2 Type II, KMS/BYOK, VPC peering, Dedicated vs Hosted, SLA Exhibit, burst capacity, committed capacity pricing, service credits.

Shared artifacts pointer: "Redwood: MSA template + DPA + Service Level Exhibit (link to secure shared folder)" (to be sent after call).
